title: Shake It!
statementMd:
*A never-ending, fast-changing and dream-like world unfolds, as the secret door opens.*

A world is an unordered graph $*G*$, in whose vertex set $*V*(*G*)$ there are two special vertices $*s*(*G*)$ and $*t*(*G*)$. An initial world has vertex set ${*s*(*G*), *t*(*G*)}$ and an edge between them.

A total of $*n*$ changes took place in an initial world. In each change, a new vertex $*w*$ is added into $*V*(*G*)$, **an existing edge** $(*u*, *v*)$ is chosen, and two edges $(*u*, *w*)$ and $(*v*, *w*)$ are added into $*E*(*G*)$. Note that it's possible that some edges are chosen in more than one change.

It's known that the capacity of the minimum $*s*$-$*t*$ cut of the resulting graph is $*m*$, that is, at least $*m*$ edges need to be removed in order to make $*s*(*G*)$ and $*t*(*G*)$ disconnected.

Count the number of *non-similar worlds* that can be built under the constraints, modulo $10^{9} + 7$. We define two worlds similar, if they are isomorphic and there is isomorphism in which the $*s*$ and $*t*$ vertices are not relabelled. Formally, two worlds $*G*$ and $*H*$ are considered similar, if there is a bijection between their vertex sets ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/092bb10f014913156786c9ab646277ac1ec2dc3a.png), such that:

- $*f*(*s*(*G*)) = *s*(*H*)$;
- $*f*(*t*(*G*)) = *t*(*H*)$;
- Two vertices $*u*$ and $*v*$ of $*G*$ are adjacent in $*G*$ if and only if $*f*(*u*)$ and $*f*(*v*)$ are adjacent in $*H*$.

## Input

The first and only line of input contains two space-separated integers $*n*$, $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 50$) — the number of operations performed and the minimum cut, respectively.

## Output

Output one integer — the number of *non-similar worlds* that can be built, modulo $10^{9} + 7$.

## Note

In the first example, the following $6$ worlds are pairwise non-similar and satisfy the constraints, with $*s*(*G*)$ marked in green, $*t*(*G*)$ marked in blue, and one of their minimum cuts in light blue.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b7002cc727dc04048daff54a7d43f3f66046f208.png)

In the second example, the following $3$ worlds satisfy the constraints.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bededb806c3fcd95b885e9610f95c0b3d406b2d5.png)
statementZhMd:
*随着秘密之门打开，一个永不停息、瞬息万变且如梦似幻的世界展现在眼前。*

一个世界是一个无序图 $*G*$，其顶点集 $*V*(*G*)$ 中有两个特殊顶点 $*s*(*G*)$ 和 $*t*(*G*)$。初始世界的顶点集为 ${*s*(*G*), *t*(*G*)}$，且两者之间有一条边。

在初始世界中共进行了 $*n*$ 次变化。每次变化中，向 $*V*(*G*)$ 添加一个新顶点 $*w*$，选择一条**已有的边** $(*u*, *v*)$，并将两条边 $(*u*, *w*)$ 和 $(*v*, *w*)$ 加入 $*E*(*G*)$。注意，同一条边可能在多次变化中被选中。

已知所得图的最小 $*s*$-$*t*$ 割的容量为 $*m*$，也就是说，至少需要删除 $*m*$ 条边才能使 $*s*(*G*)$ 和 $*t*(*G*)$ 不连通。

求在满足条件的情况下可以构造出的*互不相似的世界*数量，答案对 $10^{9} + 7$ 取模。如果两个世界同构，且存在一个同构映射不重新标记 $*s*$ 和 $*t*$ 顶点，则称这两个世界相似。形式化地，若存在顶点集之间的双射 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/092bb10f014913156786c9ab646277ac1ec2dc3a.png)，满足以下条件，则称两个世界 $*G*$ 和 $*H*$ 相似：

- $*f*(*s*(*G*)) = *s*(*H*)$；
- $*f*(*t*(*G*)) = *t*(*H*)$；
- $*G*$ 中的两个顶点 $*u*$ 和 $*v*$ 在 $*G*$ 中相邻，当且仅当 $*f*(*u*)$ 和 $*f*(*v*)$ 在 $*H*$ 中相邻。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行也是唯一一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$、$*m*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 50$），分别表示执行的操作次数和最小割。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——满足条件的*互不相似的世界*数量，答案对 $10^{9} + 7$ 取模。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，以下 $6$ 个世界两两不相似且满足条件，其中 $*s*(*G*)$ 顶点标记为绿色，$*t*(*G*)$ 顶点标记为蓝色，其最小割之一标记为浅蓝色。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b7002cc727dc04048daff54a7d43f3f66046f208.png)

在第二个样例中，以下 $3$ 个世界满足条件。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/bededb806c3fcd95b885e9610f95c0b3d406b2d5.png)
